sources.entry: imbalanced-learn - Resampling techniques for imbalanced datasets, compatible with scikit-learn.

summary.one_liner: imbalanced-learn is a Python package of resampling techniques for datasets with strong between-class imbalance, designed to work with scikit-learn.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes imbalanced-learn as a Python package offering a number of re-sampling techniques commonly used on datasets with strong class imbalance. It is compatible with scikit-learn and is part of the scikit-learn-contrib projects. The README points to external documentation for installation, API reference, and examples, and says the algorithms are detailed there. It lists minimum versions for required dependencies (Python, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, pytest) and optional ones (pandas, TensorFlow, Keras, plus Matplotlib and Seaborn for examples). The README does not enumerate the specific resampling algorithms in its text.
use_cases: oversample minority class before training a classifier
undersample majority class in skewed datasets
build scikit-learn pipelines with resampling steps
improve classifier decision boundaries on imbalanced data
notable: Compatible with scikit-learn and part of scikit-learn-contrib
Provides a range of resampling techniques for class imbalance
Endorses Scientific Python SPEC 0 minimum dependency recommendations
Citable JMLR paper for scientific use
caveats: The README does not list the individual resampling algorithms; details are in the external documentation
Several optional dependencies (TensorFlow, Keras) have their own minimum versions to satisfy
